• Global sea surface temperature increased during the 20th century and continues to rise. From 1901 through 2023, temperature rose at an average rate of 0.14°F per decade. The year 2023 was the warmest ever recorded.
  • Like air temperatures on land, the surface temperature of the world’s oceans is projected to continue to increase under all four greenhouse gas emissions scenarios. Sea surface temperatures could stabilize by late in this century under the low emissions scenario, where there are significant reductions in greenhouse gas and other air pollutant emissions. They will continue to increase under the other three scenarios, however. Higher emissions lead to higher temperatures.
